title: Williams v. South Texas Presbytery
disposition_detail: The SJC approved the panel's action: the complaint was dismissed as judicially out of order, with no merits disposition. The source attributes the dismissal to the parties' inability to agree on the Record of the Case.
first_summary: In Case 1996-06, the SJC approved the panel's dismissal of Robert Williams's complaint against South Texas Presbytery as judicially out of order because the parties could not agree on the Record of the Case. The underlying complaint and its merits are not described in the sparse source.
summary: The Standing Judicial Commission approved the panel's action dismissing Robert Williams's complaint against South Texas Presbytery as judicially out of order. The adopted reason was that the parties could not agree on the Record of the Case. The source does not describe the challenged Presbytery action, the complaint's specifications, or any merits ruling.
